title: Delay-gain driven multi-candidate gate sizing to eliminate critical-path slew degradation
hypothesis: Timing-critical paths across all benchmark designs suffer from severe transition slew degradation because SizeUpGenerator penalizes higher drive strengths by dividing delay gain by the cell area inflation ratio, forcing minimally sized replacements (X2) or leaving gates at X1. Furthermore, SizeUpGenerator generates only a single candidate per target, so any local placement legalization failure aborts sizing completely. By scoring candidate cells on timing-critical paths by pure stage delay reduction and returning a ranked multi-candidate set of viable drive strengths, the optimizer can evaluate and commit higher drive strengths (X4/X8) while gracefully falling back if OpenDP legalization fails. This directly sharpens transition slews on critical drivers and reduces both WNS and TNS.

evaluator.lesson: Candidate 0003 produced no timing evidence because the upsizeCell-to-upsizeCells API change broke test compilation, and all ten smoke logs failed during helper initialization.
evaluator.dead_end: Repeating the incompatible API rename without migrating callers will fail gates before timing evaluation.
bad_changes: SizeUpGenerator.hh replaced upsizeCell with upsizeCells while TestResizer.cc retained the old API, producing five compiler errors.
Smoke success reporting accepted ten logs containing missing helpers.tcl errors.
